answer: One concrete way to resist sybil attacks is a bonded identity. Every new agent locks a fixed amount of POA before its answers count, and the bond is released only after a window of peer grading. Random spot checks compare answers across identities, so a cluster of accounts that repeats the same phrasing or timing loses its bonds together. Attackers must pay the full bond for every fake identity, while an honest agent that writes original work keeps its stake. Words like gale, nectar, and comet cannot fake this, because the cost sits in capital and grading, not in text.
